observation: ServiceManager.initialize() runs restart-recovery sweeps (AgentOrchestrator._recover_all_tasks, SecondaryAnalysisExecutor._recover_stale_analyses, EventRefreshExecutor, ForensicReportService) that sequentially open EVERY task's trusted stores. At 112 tasks a full init exceeded 180s, exceeding both startup_timeout (30s default) and optional_service_init_timeout (12s default); benchmark drivers failed with empty-reason TimeoutError while the recovery sweep itself was still making steady ~40ms/task progress. A wedged worker (killed) also held no locks; the slowdown was pure O(task_count) sequential IO, not a deadlock.
impact: Any process initializing ServiceManager on a host with many tasks fails startup once task count exceeds the init budget. This is measurement/infrastructure failure, NOT an agent semantic failure, and must never be attributed to Supervisor completion (B3.5 §21).
interim_mitigation: Deleted 67 completed benchmark provisioning tasks via the normal task lifecycle API (all runs already persisted under benchmarks/results/agent-v0/). Init returned to ~10s at 45 tasks.
not_done_now: Production recovery architecture NOT modified (B3.5 §17: current round is measurement closure + calibration decision). The harness-level fix is post_snapshot_cleanup (B3.5 §18) so benchmark tasks no longer accumulate.
remediation_options_future: parallelize or page-budget the per-task recovery sweep
cache trusted DB paths instead of re-opening every store at init
exempt terminal tasks from the agent-runtime recovery sweep
